title: FTC Consumer Advice: Auto Repair Basics
summary: Describes what a written estimate should identify, that a shop should get authorization before work, the difference between new, remanufactured or rebuilt, and salvage parts, common noises and symptoms a driver may notice, and repair warranties. Motivates AR01, AR02, AR03, AR04, AR05, AR07, and AR08 as readings of shop and customer text; this is motivation for the patterns, not evidence of Jev performance.

title: FTC Consumer Advice: Warranties
summary: Explains written, spoken, and implied warranties, that a warranty is a promise to stand behind a product, and that reporting a defect during the warranty period obliges the company to correct it. Motivates AR06 as a classification of a narrative against a supplied policy text; coverage stays with the administrator. Motivation only, not evidence of Jev performance.

title: Wikipedia: Check engine light
summary: Encyclopedic overview of the malfunction indicator lamp as a dashboard warning that a driver reports and a technician reads with a scan tool. Motivates the warning_light category in AR01 and the flashing-light sign in AR02; motivation only, not evidence of Jev performance.

title: Wikipedia: Remanufacturing
summary: Defines remanufacturing as rebuilding a used product to original specifications with reused, repaired, and new parts, and notes rebuilt vehicular parts as a recognized category. Motivates the remanufactured label in AR05; motivation only, not evidence of Jev performance.

title: California Bureau of Automotive Repair: Maintenance and repairs
summary: A state regulator's public guidance that an estimate shows parts and labor, that the customer must authorize repairs before work begins, that the invoice lists parts that are used, reconditioned, or rebuilt, and that a warranty covers defects but not parts that wear down with normal use. Motivates AR02, AR03, AR04, AR05, AR06, AR07, and AR08; the jurisdiction's rules stay in code. Motivation only, not evidence of Jev performance.
